stack: Node.js 20+ / TypeScript / ESM / Vitest / SQLite / Apple Container or Docker

principles.rule: All TypeScript imports must use .js extension (ESM requirement), even when importing .ts source files

API keys and secrets must NEVER be passed to containers directly. All AI/external API calls from containers must route through the credential proxy (port 3001). Containers receive a placeholder credential only.
All database access must go through src/db.ts exported functions. No raw SQL or direct better-sqlite3 calls in other modules.
src/config.ts may only export non-secret configuration values read from env. Secrets belong exclusively in credential-proxy.ts.
Channels must use the self-registration pattern: call registerChannel(name, factory) at module load. Factory returns null when credentials are missing — never throw.
All container mount paths must be validated against the mount allowlist (mount-security.ts) before spawning containers. Never bypass mount security or accept mount paths from IPC payloads.
Never use bare catch blocks or catch(e: any). Always type or narrow errors. ESLint plugin no-catch-all enforces this.
Always use structured logging: logger.info({ key: value }, 'message'). Never use console.log in src/. Logger instance is in src/logger.ts.
Test files must be colocated with source files (foo.test.ts next to foo.ts). No separate test directory.

IPC command authorization must be based on the source group's directory identity (not the payload). Non-main groups cannot message other groups, register groups, or schedule tasks for other groups. isMain cannot be set via IPC payload.
When processing messages, save the previous cursor before advancing it. Roll back the cursor on agent error ONLY if no output was sent to the user (to prevent duplicate messages on retry).
Do not add abstractions, helpers, or utilities for one-time operations. Minimum complexity for current task. Three similar lines is better than a premature abstraction.
Prefer editing existing files over creating new ones. Only create new files when clearly necessary (new channel, new module, new skill).

Only groups with isMain: true have unrestricted trigger access and can execute privileged operations (register groups, schedule tasks for other groups, send messages to other groups, use remote control).

IPC email attachments must be specified as container paths (/workspace/group/...). The host resolves them to groups/{groupFolder}/... and verifies file existence before sending. Never accept absolute host paths from agents.
